issues.description: Attribute 'name' of class Animal is specified inconsistently across the exercise artifacts: the UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 26-29) shows 'name: String', while the textual task instructions (problem_statement.md lines 80-86) explicitly require using StringBuilder for the name attribute. The reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 4) implements the field as 'private String name;'. This three-way mismatch (UML vs. textual requirement vs. solution) will confuse students about the expected type for the Animal.name field and whether getters/setters should expose a StringBuilder or a String. It may also lead to unnecessary edits when comparing student code with the reference solution or when writing tests that assume one type or the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected type for Animal.name consistent across all artifacts. Two clear options: (A) If StringBuilder is the intended teaching point, update the UML in problem_statement.md to 'name: StringBuilder', update the template and solution Animal class to use a private StringBuilder name field, adjust the constructor and setter accordingly, and (optionally) document whether getName() should return String (name.toString()) or the StringBuilder. (B) If a plain String was intended, remove the StringBuilder requirement from the textual instructions and keep the UML and solution using String. Prefer explicitly documenting the chosen API (field type and getter return type) in the problem statement so students know what to implement and what the reference solution expects.
